Deut. 21, 15. 24, 2. δ) הָיָה כְּ to be or

וִהְיִיתֶם כֵּאלֹהִים and ye shall become as

Comp. Is. 10, 9. 20, 6; where הָיָה is
omitted.
3. to be, i. e. the substantive verb, like
Gr. εἰμί, Lat. sum. a) As the copulative
connecting the subject with the predi-
cate; whether the latter be an adjective,
noun, numeral, or adverb; or whether it
stand alone, or in connection with a par-
ticle. So with an adjective, Gen. 3, 1
וְהַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה עָרוּם and the serpent was
cunning. 2, 25. With a substantive,
Gen. 3, 20 כִּי הִיא הָיְתָה אֵם כָּל־חָי for she
was the mother of all living. 5, 32. 16, 12.
With a subst. and numeral, Gen. 5, 5
and all the days of Adam.... were nine
hundred and thirty years. v. 8. 11. Job
1, 3. With an adverb, Gen. 15, 5 כֵּן
יִהְיֶה זַרְעֶךָ so shall thy seed be. With a
subst. having the prefix כְּ, Ps. 22, 15 הָיָה
לִבִּי כַדּוֹנָג my heart is like wax. Is. 1, 18.
30. 9, 18. In very many examples of
this kind the substantive verb may be
omitted; and indeed is more frequently
omitted than inserted; see Lehrg. p. 849.
But the rules laid down as to its use by
Ewald are too narrow; Krit. Gr. p. 632.
Kl. Gr. § 571. 2. b) As expressing
the being or remaining in any place or
state; Gen. 4, 8 וַיְהִי בִּהְיוֹתָם בַּשָּׂדֶה and it
came to pass when they were in the field,
pr. in their being in the field. 13, 3. 17,
13. Is. 7, 23. Gen. 2, 18 לֹא טוֹב הֱיוֹת הָאָדָם
לְבַדּוֹ it is not good for man to be alone.
Ecc. 7, 14. c) Emphatic; to be in exist-
ence, to exist, e. g. in some place, Gen. 2, 5
שִׂיחַ הַשָּׂדֶה טֶרֶם יִהְיֶה בָאָרֶץ the plants of
the field were not yet in the earth, did not
yet exist. 6, 4. Is. 11, 16. Absol. Gen.
13, 7 וַיְהִי רִיב and there was strife. 15,
17 עֲלָטָה הָיָה there was darkness. Zech.

Hom. Od. 15. 432; οὐ δὴν ἦν Il. 6. 131.
Matt. 2, 18. So Job 3, 16 as a hidden
untimely birth לֹא אֶהְיֶה I had not been,
should not have existed, lived. Is. 23, 13.
The following constructions and phra-
ses may also be noted: aa) הָיָה קֹטֵל,
he was slaying, for he slew; comp. Syr.
ܩܳܛܶܠ ܗܘܳܐ. Gen. 4, 17 וַיְהִי בֹּנֶה and he
was building. 15, 17 וַיְהִי הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בָּאָה
and the sun was going down. Is. 10, 14.
Often in the later writers, Job 1, 14.
Neh. 1. 4. 2, 13. 15. bb) הָיָה לְ, to be to
any one, i. e. to belong to, and with a per-
sonal subject, to have. Gen. 12, 16 וַיְהִי
לוֹ צֹאן וּבָקָר and he had sheep and oxen.
Ex. 20, 3 לֹא־יִהְיֶה לְךָ אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים thou
shalt have no other gods. Gen. 13, 5.
2 Sam. 12, 2. Is. 5, 1; לְ omitted 2 Sam.
4, 2. Comp. יֶשׁ לִי, Gr. ἔστι μοι, Arab.
كان لى est mihi, i. q. habeo, Cor. 10. 100.
cc) Also הָיָה לְ, to be for any thing, i. e.
to serve as or for any thing, to be any
thing, Gr. εἶναι εἴς τι, γένεσθαι εἴς τι.
Gen. 1, 15 וְהָיוּ לִמְאוֹרֹת and they shall
be for lights. v. 14. 29. Is. 1, 14 הָיוּ עָלַי
לָטֹרַח they are to me for a burden. With
לְ c. inf. Is. 5, 5 וְהָיָה לְבָעֵר and it shall
be for consuming, burning, pr. Eng. it
shall be to burn. With a dat. of pers.
Gen. 6, 21 וְהָיָה לְךָ וְלָהֶם לְאָכְלָה and it
shall be to thee and to them for food. Ex.
4, 16 הוּא יִהְיֶה לְּךָ לְפֶה וְאַתָּה תִּהְיֶה לּוֹ
לֵאלֹהִים he shall be to thee for a mouth,
and thou shalt be to him for God, i. e.
he shall speak in public whatever thou
shalt suggest to him in private.—
Sometimes הָיָה לְ is i. q. to show oneself
so and so, to acquit oneself as; 1 Sam.
4, 9 הִתְחַזְּקוּ וִהְיוּ לַאֲנָשִׁים be strong and
quit yourselves like men. So with לְ
twice, 1 Sam. 18, 17 הֱיֵה־לִי לְבֶן־חַיִל be
thou valiant for me, pr. quit thyself for
me as a man of valour. dd) The for-
mula הָיָה לַעֲשׂוֹת has a double signif.

line_status.note: Running-header catchwords are printed unpointed: no qamets or any vowel point appears under either היה, so Reading A's pointing is not on the page.
Final letter is a final nun ן with a clear descender below the baseline (not he ה), and the kaf has tsere (two dots) beneath it, no holem above — so כֵּן as in Reading A, not כֹּה.
The kaph of כַדּוֹנָג is printed without a dagesh (patach only); the sole dagesh in the word is in the dalet. Reading A adds a dagesh in the kaph that is not printed.

Printed Syriac is pointed (so B's unpointed ܡܬܠ ܗܘܐ is wrong, and its letters are wrong), but the rightmost-printed word is ܩܳܛܶܠ and ܗܘܳܐ stands leftmost, so in logical order it is ܩܳܛܶܠ ܗܘܳܐ, the reverse of A's order.

The print shows dagesh dots in the lamed of לְּךָ, the tav of תִּהְיֶה and the lamed of לּוֹ (matching MT Ex 4:16 pointing); Reading A omits all three. Otherwise both readings match the print, including the defective/plene spellings and the number "4, 16".
